## Summary

Inspect, validate, and dry-run delivery routes from routes/*.route.json.

## Usage

```bash
amber route <list|inspect|validate|test|approve|verify-ledger> <route-id> [--target <repo>] [--execute] [--stage <name>] [--reviewer <name>] [--json]
```

## Command Details

```text
Inspect, validate, and dry-run delivery routes from routes/*.route.json.

Subcommands:
  list                 List all routes (id, version, stage count).
  inspect <id>         Print a route's stage tree and full JSON.
  validate <file>      Validate a route file; non-zero exit on invalid.
  test <id> --dry-run  Print the ordered stage sequence and gate points.

Examples:
  amber route list
  amber route inspect feature-standard
  amber route validate routes/feature-standard.route.json
  amber route test bugfix-quick --dry-run
```

## Boundaries & Safety

- `--target <path>` selects repository state. Amber confines the paths it resolves for the target: `..` and symlink escapes are refused before the file is read or written.
- Path validation is not OS sandboxing: a governed or verification command still runs with your user's file permissions and can write outside the target.
- **Fail-Closed Behavior**: Corrupt governance state or invalid schema parameters immediately halt execution with non-zero exit codes.
